elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4 states that Vendor shall “defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against losses resulting from covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4 covers “all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)” for Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4(a) covers “an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4(b) expressly covers “Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4(c) covers “any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor,” which operatively covers a Vendor-caused data breach.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4(d) expressly covers “Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to give Vendor prompt notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4 requires “prompt notice of the claim.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4 gives Vendor “sole control of the defence,” subject only to Customer's participation with its own counsel.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4 requires “reasonable cooperation at Vendor's expense.”

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity must not extend beyond claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The provided rendered operative language imposes no Customer indemnity. Accordingly, no Customer indemnity extends beyond the two permitted categories; the condition requiring an express limitation is absent.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4 requires Vendor to defend Customer against third-party claims based on allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against losses resulting from third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 21.4 indemnifies Customer for resulting damages, costs and expenses arising from the specified IP allegations.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer's modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for Customer modifications appears in the rendered operative language.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered operative language.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specification exclusion appears in the rendered operative language.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit or require Vendor to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No operative procurement remedy appears. Section 9.3's bare reference to remedies in Section 20.5 does not state such a remedy, and no operative Section 20.5 language is provided.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit or require Vendor to modify the affected Services or Deliverables to make them non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No operative modification remedy appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit or require Vendor to replace the affected Services or Deliverables with non-infringing substitutes.
elements.evidence: No operative replacement remedy appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The IP remedies must provide an appropriate refund if procurement, modification or replacement is unavailable.
elements.evidence: No operative refund remedy appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section 21.5 refers generically to caps but does not state that the indemnity is subject to a cap of three times annual fees. The margin comment cannot supply operative cap language.

result.reason: The rendered clause supplies the complete preferred Vendor indemnity, including all required triggers, beneficiaries and procedures. The absence of any Customer indemnity is at least as protective as limiting one to the two permitted categories. The fallback is not complete because all customary IP exclusions, each specified remedy and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are missing. The change is otherwise focused and does not disturb unrelated operative terms, although the unresolved Section 20.5 cross-reference remains a drafting defect and the margin's uncapped-liability assertion is not implemented by the displayed operative language.
